questions.question: What is the relationship between angle of attack and lift on an aircraft wing?

choices.A: Lift increases linearly with angle of attack indefinitely
choices.B: Lift increases with angle of attack until critical angle, then decreases sharply
choices.C: Angle of attack has no effect on lift
choices.D: Lift is proportional to the square of the angle of attack

questions.explanation: As angle of attack increases, lift increases initially. However, beyond the critical angle of attack, the airflow separates and lift decreases sharply (stall).
steps: 1. Understand aerodynamic principles: angle of attack affects airflow.
2. Recognize the lift curve: lift increases then decreases.
3. Know the critical angle: beyond this point, stall occurs.
questions.fastStrategy: Lift curve: increases, peaks at critical angle, then drops sharply at stall.

questions.question: What is induced drag?

choices.A: Drag caused by air friction on the fuselage
choices.B: Drag caused by the wing generating lift
choices.D: Drag that occurs only at high speeds

questions.explanation: Induced drag is the drag created as a side effect of the wing generating lift. It is inseparable from lift production.
steps: 1. Understand drag types: parasitic and induced.
2. Recall induced drag definition: created by lift generation.
3. Eliminate fuselage friction (parasitic), engine (not drag), speed-only (occurs at all speeds).
questions.fastStrategy: Induced drag = drag caused by lift; cannot have lift without it.
